- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days — cap forecast at +5% above peak or align with 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.7) and price is trending up, model underestimates mean reversion — adjust downward by 2–5% in 10–15 day horizon.
- Model overestimates short-term volatility when sentiment is mixed — smooth 30d forecast by applying 3-point moving average or reduce standard deviation by 15–20%.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.65 → -0.27 → +0.63), model fails to anticipate mean reversion — apply 10-day lag correction: subtract 0.5–1.0 from forecast if sentiment flips from positive to negative.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70, model tends to overpredict — apply downward bias of 2–4% if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
